reason: The bone picture shows spaces awaiting mineral, so adding it directly addresses the strengthening goal.
expectation: The mineral will fill the spaces and strengthen the living bones.

alternatives.reason: Building a muscle is another clear goal, but I will strengthen the bones first.

effect: The mineral strengthened the bones while leaving the joint's soft tissues intact. Next I can build a muscle between the tendon attachments.
reaction: It was useful to see that the joint stays free to move.
reason: The front attachments have a space for muscle cells, matching the goal of building muscles on both sides of the elbow.
expectation: The muscle cells will form a muscle between the front tendon attachments.

alternatives.reason: The back attachments also need a muscle, so I could start there instead.

effect: The front muscle became the biceps, which pulls to bend the elbow; the back attachments still need a muscle.
reaction: The picture made the connection between attachment position and bending clearer.
reason: The back attachments have the remaining space for muscle cells, matching the goal of building muscles on opposite sides.
expectation: The cells will form a muscle behind the elbow that pulls in the opposite direction.

effect: The back muscle became the triceps and straightens the elbow. Its attachment position, rather than a different kind of muscle cell, explains the opposite movement.
reaction: The comparison with the biceps made the two pulling directions clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the biceps and triceps was most worthwhile because their positions showed how muscles pulling across opposite sides can bend and straighten the elbow.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding mineral was straightforward and less of a decision, though the result usefully explained hardness and the joint staying movable.

surprise.text: The same kind of muscle cells could form muscles that produce opposite movements because their attachments differ.

arbitrary.text: None felt arbitrary: the pictures showed spaces for the mineral and muscle cells, and the goals explained what to build.

continue.text: I would choose to try another chapter: seeing how the attachment positions changed movement made me curious about how other body parts work together.
